anf_compare.notes: No published English was consulted; translated from the PG 70 Greek only.

bible_refs.note: The trampled pasture and muddied water take up LXX Ezekiel 34:18 (τὰ κατάλοιπα τῆς νομῆς ὑμῶν κατεπατεῖτε ... τὸ λοιπὸν τοῖς ποσὶν ὑμῶν ἐταράσσετε); Cyril uses κατεπάτουν and συνετάραττον.
Lemma Καὶ ἀναστήσω ἐπ' αὐτοὺς ποιμένα ἕνα ... τὸν δοῦλόν μου Δαβίδ = LXX Ezekiel 34:23 (ποιμένα ἕνα καὶ ποιμανεῖ αὐτούς, τὸν δοῦλόν μου Δαυιδ); the catena's ellipsis stands for the omitted words.

choices.term: οὐκ ἀνικάνως ἔχουσαν ποδηγεῖν εἰς ἀλήθειαν
choices.english: which was well able to guide them to the truth
choices.why: Litotes: 'not unable' means 'well able'. The earlier draft reversed the sense.
rejected: was not unconquerably able to guide to truth

choices.term: παχεῖάν τινα καὶ ὑλώδη καὶ γαιώδους ἀκαθαρσίας ἀνάπλεων παρατιθέντες διδασκαλίαν
choices.english: setting a thick, material teaching, full of earthly impurity, before
choices.why: The adjectives agree with διδασκαλίαν, the object of παρατιθέντες ('setting before'); impurity is what the teaching is full of, not the object.
rejected: setting forth a thick and earthly impurity

choices.term: τοῖς ἐν τάξει προβάτων ἀκολουθοῦσιν αὐτοῖς ὡς κριοῖς
choices.english: those who followed them as sheep follow rams
choices.why: The dative participle names those who receive the teaching; ἐν τάξει προβάτων is 'in the place of sheep', and the Levites are the rams.
rejected: teaching the sheep to follow them like rams

choices.why: ἀταλαίπωρος is 'without trouble'; with ἰδεῖν it means plain or easy to see.
rejected: a thing to be seen without weariness

edition.locus: Frag remainder, close ('and fine, clear water' to 'already been done')

pass_a_gloss: [continuing: those of the blood of Levi, having as it were a most beautiful pasture] and fine and transparent (διειδές) having water, the instruction (παίδευσιν) through Moses, not unable (οὐκ ἀνικάνως) to guide into truth, they trampled in a way the pasture; and they stirred up also the water, a thick and material (ὑλώδη) and of earthy impurity full teaching (διδασκαλίαν) setting before (παρατιθέντες) those in the rank of sheep following them as rams. Lemma: and I will raise up over them one shepherd ... my servant David [Ezekiel 34:23]. [Cat. f. 225] That he says such things about Christ, untroublesome (ἀταλαίπωρον) to see; for having died before already the blessed David and in tombs already lying, prophesied on the one hand the blessed Ezekiel. And was making the promise (ὑπόσχεσιν) the God and Father as going to be according to times, and not as already fulfilled; for on things going to be the promises, no longer on things already done.
pass_b_english: …and fine, clear water, namely the instruction given through Moses, which was well able to guide them to the truth, in a way trampled the pasture and muddied the water as well (Ezekiel 34:18), setting a thick, material teaching, full of earthly impurity, before those who followed them as sheep follow rams.

“And I will raise up over them one shepherd … my servant David” (Ezekiel 34:23). That he says such things about Christ is easy to see. For when the blessed David had already died and was already lying in the tomb, the blessed Ezekiel prophesied; and God the Father made the promise as one that would come to pass in due time, not as one already fulfilled. For promises concern what is yet to be, not what has already been done.
source_text:
λεπτὸν δὲ καὶ διειδὲς ἔχοντες ὕδωρ τὴν διὰ Μωϋσέως παίδευσιν οὐκ ἀνικάνως
ἔχουσαν ποδηγεῖν εἰς ἀλήθειαν, κατεπάτουν τρόπον τινὰ τὴν νομήν· συνετάραττον
δὲ καὶ τὸ ὕδωρ, παχεῖάν τινα καὶ ὑλώδη καὶ γαιώδους ἀκαθαρσίας ἀνάπλεων
παρατιθέντες διδασκαλίαν τοῖς ἐν τάξει προβάτων ἀκολουθοῦσιν αὐτοῖς ὡς κριοῖς.
Καὶ ἀναστήσω ἐπ' αὐτοὺς ποιμένα ἕνα ... τὸν δοῦλόν μου ∆αβίδ. Cat. f. 225.) Ὅτι δὲ
περὶ Χριστοῦ τὰ τοιαῦτά φησιν, ἀταλαίπωρον ἰδεῖν· προτετελευτηκότος γὰρ ἤδη τοῦ
μακαρίου ∆αβὶδ καὶ ἐν τάφοις ἤδη κειμένου, προεφήτευσε μὲν ὁ μακάριος Ἰεζεκιήλ.
Ἐποιεῖτο δὲ τὴν ὑπόσχεσιν ὁ Θεὸς καὶ Πατὴρ ὡς ἐσομένην κατὰ καιροὺς, καὶ οὐχ ὡς
ἤδη τετελεσμένην· ἐπὶ γὰρ τοῖς ἐσομένοις αἱ ὑποσχέσεις, οὐκέτι τοῖς ἤδη
πεπραγμένοις.

reviewer: claude (Wave A review, clause by clause against the Greek)
review_notes: The earlier machine draft is replaced by the reviewed English from rv0; it had reversed the litotes οὐκ ἀνικάνως, made the instruction the subject, dropped the teaching (διδασκαλίαν), misread the sheep-and-rams clause and ἀταλαίπωρον, calqued προεφήτευσε μέν, and lost 'the Father'.
The lemma is now quoted and cited (Ezekiel 34:23), and the trampled pasture and muddied water are cited to Ezekiel 34:18; the rams may echo Ezekiel 34:17 but are left uncited.
bible_refs, choices, lemmas and Pass A rewritten to match; the old lemma tags παιδεία, ποδηγεώ and νόμη corrected to παίδευσις, ποδηγέω and νομή.
Translator notes on the English row replaced; the old note about the previous draft was worksheet text and its gloss was wrong.
The trailing '1' in the source is a page number and is not translated.
